records.issue_text: Test cleanup registers removal against wrong alias 'alias' instead of the actual created aliases (idp-alias-0..20), leaking all 22 created IDPs into the shared realm
records.rationale:
In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup mistakenly registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (literal "alias") instead of the created alias. This is visible in the loop:
- `idpRep.setAlias("idp-alias-" + i);`
- `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`
So the created IDPs are not cleaned up as intended, leading to leaked IDPs in the shared test realm.

records.issue_text: Cached getForLogin collects results into a HashSet, losing the delegate's deterministic alias ordering between cache-miss and cache-hit calls
records.rationale: In the new cached implementation of `getForLogin`, the cache-hit path collects `IdentityProviderModel` into a `HashSet` (`Set<IdentityProviderModel> identityProviders = new HashSet<>(); ... identityProviders.add(idp); return identityProviders.stream();`). A `HashSet` does not preserve insertion order, so the iteration/stream order can differ from the cache-miss path, which returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(...)` directly (preserving whatever deterministic order the delegate provides). This creates observable behavioral inconsistency between cache-miss and cache-hit calls.
records.stripped_text: Cached getForLogin collects results into a HashSet, losing the delegate's deterministic alias ordering between cache-miss and cache-hit calls

records.issue_text: idp.getConfig() NPE breaks all login-provider listing when config map is null
records.rationale:
The diff adds a new condition to `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:

```java
.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
```
